minutes.headline: Personnel Committee approved several salary plan bylaw changes and two new on-call fire grades; step-date change tabled.
minutes.summary: The committee moved new business ahead of the Salary Administration Plan (SAP) bylaw review. It set a videographer's starting step and assigned grades to two new on-call fire positions. It then worked through the town attorney's recommended bylaw changes and voted on several. A proposal to tie new hires' step increases to their hire date was tabled, and the review continues on February 16th.

budget_items.what_was_said: The hire was recommended at grade three, step six, matching the last college graduate hired. Existing videographers sit at lower and higher steps.
A proposal would give new hires step increases on their hire anniversary rather than July 1. Payroll staff said that adds manual tracking and room for error.
Members debated whether SAP employees or department heads should be able to appeal to the committee rather than ending with the town manager's final decision.

decisions.decision: Heather and Julie were asked to look into whether software could handle anniversary-date step increases for new hires.
The layoff and recall procedure section was passed over until the town attorney provides language.
The overtime section's public safety calculation was flagged as a question for the attorney.
Next meeting set for Wednesday, February 16th at 5 p.m., by Zoom.
The two new fire grades are new positions and must go before town meeting for approval.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted 4-1 to approve the town attorney's changes to the personnel committee and the classification and salary schedule sections of the salary bylaw.
A proposal to give new hires step increases on their hire anniversary was tabled so staff can look for a software solution.
Two motions to remove the town manager's final and binding decision from the grievance procedure failed; the red-line grievance changes then passed with two members opposed.
The committee set a videographer's starting step and assigned grades to two new on-call fire positions, which must go before town meeting for approval.
The committee passed over the layoff and recall section until the town attorney supplies language, and continued the review to a later meeting.

why_it_matters: The Salary Administration Plan sets how town employees are paid and promoted, so these edits shape future payroll costs that reach the town budget, mostly taxes.
The two new on-call fire grades count as new positions and will appear as an article residents are asked to vote on at town meeting.
